candidate.answerReason: The equation gives a unique angle of 45°. Its supplement is 135° and its complement is 45°, satisfying the factor of 3.

methods.label: Set up an angle equation
methods.explanation: Let the angle measure \(x^\circ\). Then \(180-x=3(90-x)\), which gives \(x=45\).
methods.levelReason: Uses Grade 7 angle definitions, algebraic expressions, and a linear equation with parentheses.

methods.label: Use the 90° difference
methods.explanation: The supplement and complement are found by subtracting the same angle from \(180^\circ\) and \(90^\circ\), so their difference is \(180^\circ-90^\circ=90^\circ\). The supplement is three copies of the complement, so this difference is two copies of the complement. Therefore the complement measures \(90^\circ\div2=45^\circ\), and the angle measures \(90^\circ-45^\circ=45^\circ\).
methods.levelReason: Uses the same Grade 7 angle definitions with elementary subtraction and division, avoiding an equation.
